correctness.rationale: Reconstructed actual 12-vertex, 30-edge, 5-regular icosahedral graph and its 11 nonsink sites. Independently formed its reduced Laplacian from all 30 source edges; exact integer determinant=5,184,000, matching stated recurrent count. Read complete first C++17 enumeration: loops through all base-five 11-site stable vectors (5^11=48,828,125); Dhar burning deletion selects eligible lowest-index vertices, then stabilizes at three source distances, counting total topplings and distinct toppled vertices. Read independent second implementation with separate two-ring graph, Dhar burning-addition and reverse toppling priority; read Python verifier that compiles both, parses 100 positive CSV counters, checks exact per-class totals, zero mass and maximal mass and equality of the entire histogram. Thus claimed finite exhaustiveness has explicit reproducible loops and cross-check path; I did not run both 48-million-state programs in this execution and therefore treat the exact 100-entry census as independently inspected code-supported rather than freshly re-enumerated. Automorphism sink stabilizer acts transitively on each distance sphere, so representatives suffice. The no-repeat nearest class and coefficient palindrome come from exhaustive table, not a universal graph theorem.
